{{nihongo|'''Awa Shrine (Oyama)'''|安房神社}} is a Shinto shrine located in Awamiya, {{ill|Oyama, Tochigi|Q374511|qid=Q374511}}, {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|Q44843|qid=Q44843}}. Its former shrine rank was Gōsha, and it is listed as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} (minor shrine). {{nihongo|'''Awa Shrine (Oyama)'''|安房神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Shimotsuke Province]].

== Enshrined deities ==
* {{ill|Futodama|Q11059539|qid=Q11059539|qid=Q11059539|lt=Ame-no-Futodama-no-Mikoto}} (あめのふとだまのみこと)
* {{ill|Uji no Wakiiratsuko|Q11619989|qid=Q11619989|lt=Uji no Wakairatsuko-no-Mikoto}} (うじのわきいらつこのみこと)

== History ==
According to shrine tradition, it was founded during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|Q333530|qid=Q333530}} and rebuilt during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|Q313119|qid=Q313119}}. In the {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}, it is recorded under the name “Abo Shrine.”

In 939, it is said that Fujiwara no Hidesato prayed here for victory in his campaign against Taira no Masakado and donated shrine lands. In the medieval period, the area was known as Awamiya, and the shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Oyama clan|Q11459903|qid=Q11459903}}, {{ill|Sano clan|Q11385058|qid=Q11385058}}, {{ill|Yūki clan|Q2975399|qid=Q2975399}}, and the {{ill|Koga kubō|Q8017022|qid=Q8017022}}, among others.

== Rituals ==
Each year on November 21, a festival is held in which a mikoshi decorated with millet ears and distinctive red-and-white mizuhiki cords known as “Awamusubi” is paraded. This event is known as the “Awagara Mikoshi custom.”<ref>{{Cite book|Japanese|url=https://ndlsearch.ndl.go.jp/books/R100000002-I000008512661|editor=Association for Historical Walks in Tochigi Prefecture|title=Historical Walks of Tochigi Prefecture|year=1997|publisher=Yamakawa Publishing}}</ref>

== Cultural properties ==
== Designated Tangible Cultural Properties (City-designated) ==
* Awa Shrine documents (10 items), including the Tawara Tōta prayer text<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese|url=https://sitereports.nabunken.go.jp/ja/22542 |title=Oyama City Cultural Property Protection Survey Annual Report 17 – Comprehensive Database of Archaeological Site Reports |website=Nara National Research Institute for Cultural Properties |accessdate=2018-10-14}}</ref>
* Festival illustrated votive plaque (ema)
* Railway-themed ema (on display at the Oyama City Museum)

== Intangible Folk Cultural Properties (City-designated) ==

* Awagara Mikoshi custom<ref name=":0" />
